questions.q: What is the top level of the Unity Catalog three-level namespace?
questions.explain: Catalogs sit directly below the metastore and are the first (top) level of the catalog.schema.table namespace.

questions.q: What is the auto-created catalog every Unity Catalog-enabled workspace gets?
options: A workspace catalog, sharing the workspace's own name, accessible to its users by default
A catalog named 'default' shared across every workspace in the account
No catalog is auto-created; one must always be created manually first
A read-only catalog that cannot hold any tables
questions.explain: Every Unity Catalog workspace gets its own auto-created workspace catalog, named after the workspace, accessible to that workspace's users by default.

questions.q: A Unity Catalog schema is the same concept as what in SQL Server or PostgreSQL?
questions.explain: A schema groups tables, views, volumes, and functions the same way a database does in SQL Server/PostgreSQL — Databricks itself used to call this level 'database' before Unity Catalog's current terminology.

questions.q: What does running USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA actually change?
options: The session's default catalog/schema, so unqualified names resolve against them — the table's real name is unchanged
The table's fully-qualified name permanently, for every user
Nothing; these are deprecated, no-op statements
The metastore the session is attached to
questions.explain: USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA set session-level defaults for unqualified name resolution; the object's real, fully-qualified name is always catalog.schema.table regardless.

questions.q: What is the fully-qualified three-level name for a table called invoices in the accounts_payable schema of the finance catalog?
questions.explain: The three-level namespace is always catalog.schema.table — finance (catalog), accounts_payable (schema), invoices (table).
